transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Anna (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood CSM), Priya (Valence CTO), Ethan (Platform), Claire (Security), Jared (DevOps)

Summary (auto): quick kickoff to align access and pilot plan; action items captured.

Transcript:
[00:00] Anna: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Anna, AE on this account. Quick roundtable?
[00:12] Priya: Hi all, Priya here, CTO at Valence. We've got Ethan, Claire, Jared on.
[00:17] Ethan: Hey.
[00:18] Claire: Hi.
[00:20] Anna: Great. I'll hand it to Sofia to frame today's goals — Sofia?
[00:25] Sofia: Yeah hi, thanks. Goal is to align network and access so you can spin up the staging pilot next week, make sure security reqs are clear and we share initial perf bench plan. Keep it pretty tactical.
[00:40] Priya: Sounds good. Our timeline is tight, want to have a pilot running in staging by end of next week.
[00:47] Marcus: Awesome, we can absolutely try, just want to set expectations around the variables — if you go dedicated GPUs vs hosted there's an ops lead time and also provisioning windows.
[00:58] Jared: Quick q, when you say "staging pilot" — is that a hosted sandbox in Redwood, or will we bring up a private VPC deploy?
[01:07] Anna: Good question. We typically do a hosted staging for first perf runs so we can iterate quickly, then mirror the same config for Dedicated or Private if you need isolation.
[01:16] Claire: For us, isolation matters because of PCI-adjacent data. We might need VPC peering or Private. Also KMS — we want to use our own key management.
[01:26] Marcus: Yep, KMS integrations supported for Private and Dedicated. Hosted can support customer-managed keys with HSM in specific contracts but that's usually later.
[01:35] Priya: Okay, we prefer customer-managed keys. We'll need to know the list of supported KMS vendors and HSM options.
[01:42] Marcus: We'll include that in the runbook.
[01:45] Anna: On network: Claire, can you confirm who owns the firewall/IP allowlist?
[01:52] Claire: That'll be Jared and the infra team. We'll provide an allowlist, but need the exact IP ranges and whether we need NATs.
[02:00] Marcus: For hosted staging, we provide specific egress IPs for API callbacks; for Private there's no egress required but you'll open ports for healthchecks and control plane. We'll send both patterns.
[02:13] Jared: Ok, send the pattern. Also any port numbers?
[02:16] Marcus: Mostly TLS on 443, occasionally port 8443 for internal metrics if you opt-in. We'll document.
[02:24] Priya: Great. On SSO, we use SAML with Okta. Claire will handle.
[02:29] Claire: Yep. We'll need the SP metadata and ACS URLs. Any chance those are in the runbook?
[02:34] Anna: Yes, runbook will have the SAML endpoints and metadata template.
[02:38] Marcus: Also will capture RBAC primitives — how we map IdP groups to Redwood roles.
[02:44] Priya: For success criteria: we measure latency and error rate under a 2k qps simulated load? Is that realistic?
[02:53] Marcus: 2k QPS is significant. For a pilot we'll aim for a scaled-down benchmark with the model size you picked — which model did you want to test?
[03:02] Priya: We're starting with a mid-size open model for reranking and embeddings, and then a larger chat model later.
[03:09] Marcus: Okay — important because KV-cache behavior and batching will change. We'll propose sequences for the perf run.
[03:17] Ethan: Can you share the perf spreadsheet so we can fill in traffic profiles?
[03:20] Marcus: Yep, I'll share a template — that's the perf-benchmark spreadsheet.
[03:24] Priya: On compliance, do you have SOC2 and ISO docs we can share with our security team?
[03:30] Anna: Absolutely — we'll attach SOC2 report and our security whitepaper. If you need an NDA exchange or an SCC it's fine.
[03:36] Claire: We'll want audit log retention details — how long logs are kept, whether they include token-level traces.
[03:43] Marcus: By default audits are stored 90 days, but enterprise packages can extend. Token-level traces are redacted by default unless explicitly enabled for debugging and under a contract. We'll detail that.
[03:54] Jared: A quick note: we run on a mix of GCP and on-prem infra; network egress might need peering and specific routes.
[04:02] Marcus: Noted — we'll include routing patterns for hybrid infra.
[04:06] Priya: On cost — we care about latency/cost tradeoffs; Redwood mentioned batching and quantization recommendations. Will you provide concrete guidance?
[04:15] Anna: Yes, Redwood Optimize will include batching profiles and quantization suggestions. Marcus will suggest quantization options by model family.
[04:22] Marcus: Right, for that mid-size model we can recommend int8 quantization steps; for chat models we typically keep higher precision.
[04:30] Claire: Any PII handling assurances? We need to know what is persisted and whether we can opt out of caching.
[04:36] Marcus: You can opt out of KV/prefix caching; default is cached for performance but we can disable it per-route. We'll document per-route toggles.
[04:45] Priya: Perfect. Next, rollout plan: start hosted staging -> run perf -> evaluate -> decide Dedicated vs Private. Who owns the smoke tests?
[04:56] Anna: Redwood can provide a smoke test suite and we can run it together; we'll also give scripts.
[05:02] Ethan: Good. Also, can we do a canary that routes a small portion of production traffic? Thought exercise — once we go Dedicated.
[05:10] Marcus: Yes, we have route-level rollouts and can do canary weighting. We'll provide the canary playbook.
[05:15] Priya: Ok that would be helpful.
[05:18] Sofia: I'll capture next steps: Redwood to send runbook, canary playbook, perf template. Customer to send SSO and allowlist.
[05:26] Priya: Sounds right. A couple of questions from the team — what are the SLAs for latency on Dedicated?
[05:34] Anna: Our Dedicated tiers come with latency SLOs and throughput SLAs; exact numbers depend on commit and instance type. We'll attach the SLA matrix.
[05:42] Claire: And auditability — how easy is it to pull an audit for a token session?
[05:46] Marcus: We expose audit logs via the console and API; exports are possible. We'll note redaction policy again.
[05:53] Jared: If we run the pilot on hosted and then move to Private, will the config be portable?
[05:58] Marcus: Yes, that's a core design — the same config/rollout policies work across hosted/dedicated/private. Some infra details change but the API surface remains the same.
[06:07] Priya: Ok nice. Any blockers you see right now?
[06:10] Marcus: Only that we need SSO metadata and allowlist to open access; and we need to know the model and sequence length distributions to size the bench.
[06:18] Priya: We'll get those.
[06:21] Anna: Great. Quick housekeeping on contacts and docs — we'll put the runbook, security packet, and benchmark template in a shared folder.
[06:30] Claire: Can we get legal procurement points for a standard T&Cs timeline? Procurement might need an initial MSA.
[06:35] Anna: We can share standard MSA and procurement checklist. If you want accelerated procurement we can route to our contracts rep.
[06:43] Priya: We'll loop procurement if pilot looks good.
[06:47] Sofia: Ok final recap before we close?
[06:50] Anna: Recap — Redwood: share runbook, perf template, canary playbook, SOC2 docs, SLA matrix. Valence: send SSO metadata, IP allowlist, confirm KMS requirements. Schedule perf bench for 2026-05-22.
[07:05] Priya: Yep.
[07:07] Marcus: One last thing — small gotcha we sometimes see: if you use a large context window the kernel selection changes and latency spikes; we'll recommend sequence length caps for pilot.
[07:18] Ethan: Good to note.
[07:20] Anna: All right, thank you everyone, we'll follow up with the folder and action items.
[07:25] Claire: Thanks.
[07:26] Priya: Thanks all.
[07:28] --- End of meeting ---
